title: 📘 UNIT 4: THE MIDDLE AGES AND EARLY MODERN WORLD, C. 500 TO 1750S
🏰 4.1 THE MIDDLE AGES IN EUROPE
notes: 🌍 The Middle Ages in Europe included major political, social and economic changes following the decline of the Western Roman Empire.

title: 🌑 4.1.1 DARK AGE
notes:
• The Dark Age was a period of West European history from 500 AD to 1000 AD.

• It was called the Dark Ages because Civilization declined in Western Europe during this period.

• The Western Roman Empire was destroyed by internal and external problems.

title: ⚔️ DARK AGE: INVASIONS
notes:
⭐ The Western Roman Empire faced invasions in the 5th century AD from:

• Anglo Saxons
• Franks
• Huns
• Magyars

📉 Internally, the empire suffered division and decay.

title: 🏘️ DARK AGE: CHANGES IN EUROPE
notes:
• Greco-Roman Civilization declined.

• Societies became rural.

• Cities declined.

• Feudalism became the socio-economic and political order.

• Churches, castles and palaces were built.

• Bishops and monks kept records.

• Knights practiced chivalry.

• Wars, murders and blood feuds were common.

⭐ By about 1000 AD, greater stability was returning.

title: 🏰 4.1.2 FEUDAL SOCIETY
notes:
• From 500 to 1500, a new socio-political system called feudalism emerged.

• Powerful lords and vassals became increasingly important.

• The ruling class consisted of kings, nobles, knights and higher clergy.

title: 🤝 VASSALAGE AND FIEF
notes:
• Vassalage connected a higher lord with a lower lord.

• The higher lord gave a fief to the lower lord.

• The lower lord became a vassal of the higher lord.

• Fief or feud means a piece of land.

⭐ Feudalism was a system of holding land and providing service in exchange.

title: 🏡 MANORIAL SYSTEM
notes:
• The basic units of European feudalism were manors or villages.

• The manorial lord exercised political, judicial and military power over peasants.

• Peasants, craftsmen and traders formed the mass of feudal society.

• They had little political and economic power.

title: ⛪ CHURCH AND FEUDAL SOCIETY
notes:
• West European feudal society was exploitative.

• The Church had authority over the ruling class and ordinary people.

• The Roman Catholic Church owned land.

• It was responsible for religion, education and culture.

title: 🏛️ 4.1.3 BYZANTINE EMPIRE
notes:
• The Byzantine Empire was the East Roman Empire that continued after the fall of the West Roman Empire.

• Its capital was Constantinople, modern Istanbul.

• Greek became the official language.

title: ⛪ BYZANTINE CHURCH
notes:
• The Orthodox Church was officially separated from the Roman Catholic Church in 1054.

• It became the national church of the Byzantine Empire.

• The Orthodox Church supported the emperor.

title: 💰 BYZANTINE ECONOMY AND SOCIETY
notes:
🌾 Economic base:
• Agriculture
• Trade
• Crafts

🏛️ Society was divided into:
• Emperor
• Higher clergy
• Nobility who owned land
• Peasants who cultivated the land

🏗️ Byzantine architecture was known for domes and beautifully colored glasses.

title: 👑 EMPEROR JUSTINIAN
notes:
• The Byzantine Empire was at the height of its territory and power under Emperor Justinian.

• Justinian ruled from 527 to 565 AD.

title: ⚔️ BYZANTINE EMPIRE AND THE SELJUK TURKS
notes:
• The Seljuk Turks began military occupation in Asia Minor in 1040 AD.

• The Byzantine Empire was challenged by Seljuk expansion.

• The Byzantine Empire suffered a disastrous defeat at the Battle of Manzikert in 1071.

• It lost most of Asia Minor to Seljuk Turkish rulers and later to Ottoman Turks.

title: ✝️ THE CRUSADES
notes:
• The Crusades began in the 1090s.

• Christian Europe fought the Seljuk Turks to liberate Christian holy lands.

• There were eight major Crusades.

• The First Crusade began in 1096.

• The Crusades failed to crush Muslim power in the holy lands but protected Western Europe from foreign invasions in the east.

title: 🌏 4.2 THE MIDDLE AGES IN ASIA
notes: 🌍 The Middle Ages in Asia included the rise and expansion of Islam, the expansion of the Ottoman Empire and the development of the Chinese dynastic cycle.

title: ☪️ 4.2.1 THE RISE AND EXPANSION OF ISLAM
notes:
• Islam rose in the early seventh century AD.

• Islam began in the Arabian Peninsula with the life and teaching of Prophet Mohammed in Mecca around 610 AD.

• Islam means submission to the will of Allah (God).

• Those who worship Allah are called Muslims.

title: 🕋 HEJIRA
notes:
• The Quraysh Arabs opposed Prophet Mohammed and persecuted him and his followers.

• In 622 AD, Prophet Mohammed and his followers moved from Mecca to Medina.

• This journey is called Hejira.

⭐ Hejira marked the beginning of the Islamic Calendar.

title: ⚔️ MUSLIM ARAB CONQUESTS
notes:
• The Muslim Arabs changed the political, religious and social structures of the Near East and Middle East.

• Following the death of the Prophet, Muslims came under the Umayyad and Abbasid Caliphates.

• Arab conquests established a Muslim Arab empire from North Africa and Spain in the west to Central Asia in the east.

title: 🕌 ISLAMIC EXPANSION
notes:
• The Seljuk and Ottoman Turks' military occupation of Palestine, Asia Minor and Arabia contributed to the expansion of Islam.

• Islam spread throughout areas under their control and other parts of the world.

title: 🏛️ 4.2.2 EXPANSION OF THE OTTOMAN EMPIRE
notes:
• Seljuk Turks began military occupation in Palestine, Asia Minor and Arabia in 1040.

• Ottoman Turks replaced the Seljuk Turks in the area by the end of the 13th century.

• Ottoman Turks were named after their chief Osman or Othman.

title: 🌍 OTTOMAN TERRITORIAL EXPANSION
notes:
• The Ottoman Empire was centered in present-day Turkey.

• They seized Anatolia in 1336.

• Captured Adrianople in 1356.

• Captured Salonika in 1387.

• Defeated the Serbs in 1389.

• Defeated the Bulgarians in 1393.

• By the 15th century, the Balkan Peninsula, including Greece, was predominantly conquered.

title: 🏙️ CONQUEST OF CONSTANTINOPLE
notes:
• The Ottomans conquered Constantinople in 1453.

• They renamed it Istanbul.

• Istanbul became their capital.

• Syria was conquered in 1516.

• Egypt was conquered in 1517.

• In 1529, European forces successfully defended Vienna from the Turkish attack.

title: ⚔️ JANISSARIES
notes:
• The Ottomans formed a group of highly trained soldiers called Janissaries.

• They helped spread Islam throughout the empire.

• The Ottomans gained wealth from trade.

• They controlled the trade route from Europe to Asia.

• They banned European merchants from going to the Far East.

title: 👥 OTTOMAN SOCIETY
notes:
The Ottoman Turkish society was divided into four social groups:

1️⃣ Sultan
2️⃣ Grand viziers and bureaucrats
3️⃣ Janissaries and soldiers
4️⃣ Occupational groups

🌙 The culture of the Ottoman Empire was that of the Islamic world.

title: ⚓ BATTLE OF LEPANTO
notes:
• Turkish expansion in Europe ended in 1571.

• European fleets defeated the Turkish navy at the Battle of Lepanto near Greece.

title: 🏯 4.2.3 DYNASTIC CYCLE IN CHINA
notes:
• China created a great Civilization that greatly influenced other East Asian countries, particularly Korea and Japan.

• Chinese political thought accepted the idea of a dynastic cycle.

title: ☁️ MANDATE OF HEAVEN
notes:
• A new dynasty was usually strong, ruled well and had the support of the people.

• When it became corrupt and weak, it lost the support of the people.

• It was believed to lose the Mandate of Heaven, meaning its authority and legitimacy to rule China.

• Another dynasty, often founded by a rebel, would replace it.

🔄 This process was repeated as the dynastic cycle.

title: 🏯 CHINESE DYNASTIES
notes:
• A long succession of imperial dynasties ruled China from the Qin to the Qing dynasty.

• The imperial dynastic system ended with a revolution in 1911/1912.

title: 💰 4.3 DEVELOPMENT OF EARLY CAPITALISM
notes:
• Capitalism distinguished itself from previous systems by using accumulated capital to enlarge productive capacity.

• Capital was used for productive activities rather than economically unproductive enterprises such as pyramids and cathedrals.

title: 🏙️ REVIVAL OF EUROPEAN TOWNS
notes:
• Many ancient European cities and towns had been ruined following the collapse of the Roman Empire.

• Trade slowly revived.

• Old Roman cities were restored.

• Towns became centers of production and exchange.

title: 🏭 EARLY CAPITALIST RELATIONS
notes:
• Merchants learned to buy raw materials.

• Workers manufactured products.

• Finished products were sold at the best prices.

⭐ This helped develop early capitalist relations.

title: 🚢 LONG-DISTANCE TRADE
notes:
• New long-distance international trade became important after the discoveries.

• Large profits could be made.

⚠️ Major trade problems included:
• Transport difficulties
• Insecurity caused by war and robbery
• Heavy tolls on commodities

title: 🧭 4.4 AGE OF EXPLORATIONS AND DISCOVERIES
notes:
• The Age of European explorations and discoveries occurred mainly in the 15th and 16th centuries.

• Explorations were partly initiated by the need to bypass the Ottoman Turkish blockade of the old long-distance trade route from Europe to the Far East.

title: 🧭 FACTORS ENCOURAGING EXPLORATION
notes:
⭐ Important factors included:

• European interest in long-distance trade
• New inventions such as the compass
• Better maps
• Better ships
• Growing geographical knowledge
• Economic interests
• Religious interests
• Desire for glory

title: 👑 SPONSORS OF EXPLORATION
notes:
• Prince Henry, the Navigator of Portugal supported voyages of exploration.

• Queen Isabella of Spain supported voyages of explorers.

• Spain and Portugal were leaders in exploration and discoveries during the 15th and 16th centuries.

• They were followed by Holland, Britain, France and Russia.

title: ⛵ VASCO DA GAMA
notes: • Portuguese explorer Vasco da Gama discovered a new sea route to India and the Far East in 1498.

title: 🌎 CHRISTOPHER COLUMBUS
notes:
• Christopher Columbus reached America in 1492 while serving Spain.

• He died without knowing that he had found new lands.

• The newly found land became known as America after the Italian mapmaker Amerigo Vespucci.

• The newly discovered areas became known as the New World.

title: 🌍 FERDINAND MAGELLAN
notes:
• Ferdinand Magellan was a Portuguese explorer serving Spain.

• He circumnavigated the world between 1519 and 1522.

• The newly discovered lands were later conquered and became colonies of European powers.

title: 🎨 4.5 THE RENAISSANCE
notes:
• Renaissance was an intellectual movement.

• The word Renaissance indicates the rebirth of learning.

• It began in the 14th century and ended in the 17th century.

• Renaissance began in Italy and spread to the rest of Europe.

title: 🇮🇹 RENAISSANCE IN ITALY
notes:
• Renaissance Italy was essentially an urban society.

• Renaissance was an age of recovery from the disasters of the fourteenth century.

• The revival affected politics and art.

• A new view of human beings developed.

• Individual ability became increasingly emphasized.

title: 📚 RENAISSANCE CHARACTERISTICS
notes:
⭐ Major characteristics included:

• Study of ancient Rome and Greek languages, literature and arts

• Use of reason

• Freedom of thought

• Questioning mind

• Use of vernacular or national languages such as Italian and English instead of Latin in writing

title: 📖 RENAISSANCE: LITERATURE
notes:
⭐ Important works and writers:

• Divine Comedy, Dante Alighieri
• Utopia, Thomas More
• Don Quixote, Cervantes
• German translation of the Holy Bible, Martin Luther
• Plays by William Shakespeare

title: 🎨 RENAISSANCE: ART
notes:
⭐ Leonardo da Vinci:
• Last Supper
• Mona Lisa

⭐ Michelangelo:
• Creation of Adam
• Statue of David
• Statue of Moses
• Virgin and the dead Christ

title: 🔬 RENAISSANCE: SCIENCE
notes:
• Andreas Vesalius studied human anatomy.

• Nicholas Copernicus declared that the Earth revolved around the Sun.

• Previously, it was thought that the planets revolved around the Earth.

title: 🌍 RENAISSANCE AND THE MODERN WORLD
notes:
• Renaissance influenced modern society and culture.

• It brought a new focus on humanism.

• It encouraged greater attention to human potential and scientific inquiry.

• Its influence continues in contemporary society and culture.

title: ✝️ 4.6 THE REFORMATION
notes:
• The Reformation was a religious movement that led to the emergence of Protestantism from the Catholic Church.

• It began in Germany in 1517.

• Martin Luther led the movement.

• Causes included social, political, religious and economic factors.

title: ⛪ PROTESTANT REFORMATION
notes:
• Protestant reformers supported principles of capitalism, individualism and nation-states.

• Various Protestant Churches were established.

• Jean Calvin established a Calvinist Protestant Church in Switzerland.

• Calvinist followers in France were called Huguenots.

title: 🏴 PRESBYTERIAN AND ANGLICAN CHURCHES
notes:
• John Knox developed his type of Calvinist Protestantism called Presbyterian in 1560.

• King Henry VIII and Queen Elizabeth I separated the English Protestant Church from the Roman Catholic Church in England.

• The English national church became known as the Anglican Church.

title: ✝️ COUNTER-REFORMATION
notes:
• Protestantism pushed the Catholic Church into the Counter-Reformation.

• The Catholic Church carried out reforms in response to the Protestant challenge.

• The Society of Jesus was formed in Spain by Ignatius Loyola in 1534.

• Its members were called Jesuits.

title: ⚔️ RELIGIOUS CONFLICTS
notes:
• Anti-Catholics were attacked and sometimes killed.

• German Peasants' Wars against Catholics occurred between 1524 and 1525.

• The Reformation played an important role in the Thirty Years' War from 1618 to 1648.

• The Peace of Westphalia ended the war in Germany in 1648.

title: 🏭 4.7 INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION
notes:
• Industrial Revolution means the invention and use of machines in place of hard labour.

• Machines performed work previously done by hand with simple tools and equipment.

• Europe shifted from an economy based on farming and handicrafts to an economy based on machine manufacturing in factories.

title: 🇬🇧 BEGINNING OF INDUSTRIAL REVOLUTION
notes:
• The Industrial Revolution began in Great Britain in the 1780s.

• It took several decades to spread to other Western nations.

• Great Britain became the world's first and richest industrial nation by the mid-nineteenth century.

title: 💨 STEAM POWER
notes:
• Steam power became the new form of power during the Industrial Revolution.

• It replaced early wind and water power.

• Savery developed an early steam engine in 1698.

• Newcomen developed his steam engine around 1705–1711.

• James Watt improved steam engines in 1782–1784 and adapted them for machinery.

title: 🚂 STEAM POWER AND TRANSPORT
notes:
• Steam power was applied to transportation.

• Steamboats were used on rivers.

• Steamships were used at sea.

• Steam power was eventually used for railways.

• The first railway locomotive was built in 1804.

title: 🏭 INDUSTRIAL EXPANSION
notes:
• The Industrial Revolution also occurred in the United States in 1800.

• Britain was the leading industrial nation during the early and mid-nineteenth century.

• The United States eventually surpassed Britain in industrial production.

title: 🌍 INDUSTRIALIZATION IN EUROPE
notes:
• The Industrial Revolution spread to the rest of Europe at different times and speeds.

⭐ The first countries to industrialize in continental Europe were:
• Belgium
• France
• Germany
